author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 1: NEVER OUTSHINE THE MASTER
Always make those above you feel comfortably superior. In your desire to please or impress them, do not go too far in displaying your talents, or you might accomplish the opposite -- inspire fear and insecurity. Make your masters appear more brilliant than they are, and you will attain the heights of power.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 2: NEVER PUT TOO MUCH TRUST IN FRIENDS, LEARN HOW TO USE ENEMIES
Hire a former enemy rather than a former friend, for a former friend is more likely to betray you. Friends will expect favors and grow resentful; enemies have something to prove and will work harder to earn your trust. Keep a degree of distance with all friends.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 3: CONCEAL YOUR INTENTIONS
Keep people off-balance and in the dark by never revealing the purpose behind your actions. If they don't know what you're up to, they cannot prepare a defense. Guide them far enough down the wrong path, envelop them in enough smoke, and by the time they realize your intentions, it will be too late.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 4: ALWAYS SAY LESS THAN NECESSARY
When you are trying to impress people with words, the more you say, the more common you appear and the less in control. Even if you're saying something mundane, make it appear original and distinctive. Powerful people impress and intimidate by saying less. The more you talk, the more likely you are to say something foolish.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 5: SO MUCH DEPENDS ON REPUTATION -- GUARD IT WITH YOUR LIFE
Reputation is the cornerstone of power. Through reputation alone you can intimidate and win; once it slips, however, you are vulnerable and will be attacked from all sides. Make your reputation unassailable. Meanwhile, learn to destroy your enemies by opening holes in their own reputations. Then stand aside and let public opinion hang them.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 6: COURT ATTENTION AT ALL COST
Everything is judged by its appearance; what is unseen counts for nothing. Never let yourself get lost in the crowd or buried in obscurity. Be the center of attention. Court attention by any means necessary -- controversy, spectacle, mystery. Make yourself larger than life.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 7: GET OTHERS TO DO THE WORK FOR YOU, BUT ALWAYS TAKE THE CREDIT
Use the wisdom, knowledge, and legwork of other people to further your own cause. Not only will such assistance save you valuable time and energy, it will give you a godlike aura of efficiency and speed. Never do yourself what others can do for you.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 8: MAKE OTHER PEOPLE COME TO YOU -- USE BAIT IF NECESSARY
When you force others to act, you are the one in control. It is always better to make your opponent come to you, abandoning his own plans in the process. Lure him with fabulous gains, then attack. Surrender to no one; let them come to you.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 9: WIN THROUGH YOUR ACTIONS, NEVER THROUGH ARGUMENT
Any momentary triumph you think you have gained through argument is really a Pyrrhic victory. The resentment and ill will you stir up is stronger than any momentary change of opinion. Demonstrate and prove; let the results speak for themselves.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 10: INFECTION: AVOID THE UNHAPPY AND UNLUCKY
Emotional states are as infectious as diseases. You may feel sorry for the unfortunate, but helping them will only bring you down. The unhappy and unlucky attract misfortune. Associate with the happy and fortunate instead.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 11: LEARN TO KEEP PEOPLE DEPENDENT ON YOU
To maintain your independence, you must always be needed and wanted. The more people rely on you, the more freedom you have. Make people depend on you for their happiness and prosperity, but never depend on them.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 12: USE SELECTIVE HONESTY AND GENEROSITY TO DISARM YOUR VICTIM
One sincere and honest move will cover over dozens of dishonest ones. Open-hearted gestures of honesty and generosity bring down the guard of even the most suspicious people. Once their guard is down, you can manipulate them with ease.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 13: WHEN ASKING FOR HELP, APPEAL TO PEOPLE'S SELF-INTEREST, NEVER TO THEIR MERCY OR GRATITUDE
The emphasis is on self-interest. Never appeal to people's mercy or gratitude -- those feelings are temporary and easily forgotten. Instead show them how helping you benefits them directly, and they will work tirelessly on your behalf.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 14: POSE AS A FRIEND, WORK AS A SPY
Knowing your enemy is essential. Use friendly encounters and conversations to gather information. Ask indirect questions and get people to reveal their weaknesses and intentions. By posing as a friend, you gain access to their secrets.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 15: CRUSH YOUR ENEMY TOTALLY
A half-crushed enemy will recover and take revenge. Leave them no room to retaliate. If you decide to strike, do so completely and decisively. Better to eliminate the threat entirely than to leave a wounded rival who will plot against you.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 16: USE ABSENCE TO INCREASE RESPECT AND HONOR
Too much circulation makes the price go down. The more you are seen and heard, the more common you appear. Create value through scarcity. Withdraw sometimes so that people appreciate you more when you return.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 17: KEEP OTHERS IN SUSPENDED TERROR: CULTIVATE AN AIR OF UNPREDICTABILITY
Humans are creatures of habit and predictability. When you are predictable, others can plan around you and control you. Instead, be deliberately unpredictable -- sometimes friendly, sometimes stern. This keeps others off-balance and gives you the upper hand.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 18: DO NOT BUILD FORTRESSES TO PROTECT YOURSELF -- ISOLATION IS DANGEROUS
Isolation cuts you off from information and allies, making you vulnerable. Power comes from social interaction and engagement. Do not retreat behind walls; stay connected and engaged with the world around you.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 19: KNOW WHO YOU'RE DEALING WITH -- DO NOT OFFEND THE WRONG PERSON
Different people react differently to the same actions. Some are easily offended and will seek revenge; others are forgiving. Never assume everyone reacts like you. Study your targets and understand their temperament before you act.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 20: DO NOT COMMIT TO ANYONE
Only fools rush to take sides. Commit to no one but yourself. By maintaining independence and neutrality, you become the object of competing parties' attention. Stay flexible and keep your options open.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 21: PLAY A SUCKER TO CATCH A SUCKER -- SEEM DUMBER THAN YOUR MARK
No one likes feeling stupid. Make your targets feel intelligent and superior, and they will lower their guard. Once they think they are getting the better of you, they will reveal their true intentions and weaknesses.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 22: USE THE SURRENDER TACTIC: TRANSFORM WEAKNESS INTO POWER
When you are weaker, never fight for honor's sake. Surrender instead and use the time to recover and gain strength. A strategic surrender gives you breathing room while making your opponent complacent.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 23: CONCENTRATE YOUR FORCES
Conserve your energies by concentrating them where they will have the greatest effect. Intensity beats extensity. Focus your resources and efforts on a single, decisive point rather than scattering them.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 24: PLAY THE PERFECT COURTIER
Master the art of indirection and social grace. Flatter without seeming to flatter. Be charming, adaptable, and diplomatic. The perfect courtier thrives in any environment by pleasing others while advancing their own interests.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 25: RE-CREATE YOURSELF
Do not accept the role society has assigned you. Forge a new identity that commands attention and respect. Be the master of your own image and reinvent yourself as needed. Create a powerful persona.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 26: KEEP YOUR HANDS CLEAN
Your hands must appear clean. Use others to do the dirty work and execute your plans. You are the one who benefits, but someone else takes the blame. Maintain an aura of respectability.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 27: PLAY ON PEOPLE'S NEED TO BELIEVE TO CREATE A CULTLIKE FOLLOWING
People desperately want to believe in something. Give them a cause, a vision, a leader to follow. Keep your followers entertained and inspired, and they will give you power. Promise something grand but keep it vague.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 28: ENTER ACTION WITH BOLDNESS
If you are unsure of a course of action, do not attempt it. Hesitation creates doubt and weakens your position. But once you decide, act with boldness and confidence. Boldness inspires awe and intimidates opponents.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 29: PLAN ALL THE WAY TO THE END
The ending is everything. Plan every step and take into account all possible consequences, obstacles, and twists of fortune. By planning to the end, you will not be overwhelmed by circumstances and you will know when to stop.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 30: MAKE YOUR ACCOMPLISHMENTS SEEM EFFORTLESS
Your actions should seem natural and easy, concealing the effort and practice behind them. This creates an aura of grace and power. Reveal your tricks and you will be seen as ordinary.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 31: CONTROL THE OPTIONS: GET OTHERS TO PLAY WITH THE CARDS YOU DEAL
The best deceptions are the ones that seem to give the other person a choice. Make your victims feel they are in control, but the options you offer are all favorable to you. Force them to choose between two outcomes that both serve your interests.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 32: PLAY TO PEOPLE'S FANTASIES
The truth is often unpleasant and boring. People prefer fantasy and illusion. Paint a picture of a better world and people will flock to you. Create a spectacle or a grand vision that captures their imagination.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 33: DISCOVER EACH MAN'S THUMBSCREW
Everyone has a weakness -- a thumbscrew you can turn to your advantage. Find people's emotional insecurities, needs, and desires. Once you discover what makes them tick, you can manipulate them with ease.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 34: BE ROYAL IN YOUR OWN FASHION: ACT LIKE A KING TO BE TREATED LIKE ONE
The way you present yourself determines how others treat you. Act with confidence and dignity, and others will treat you with respect. Dress and behave like someone important, and you will be perceived as important. Do not accept less than you deserve.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 35: MASTER THE ART OF TIMING
Never assume a quick victory is possible. Learn to recognize the perfect moment to act. Timing is everything -- the same action at the wrong time can fail, while at the right time it can achieve extraordinary results. Be patient, but strike decisively when the moment comes.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 36: DISDAIN THINGS YOU CANNOT HAVE: IGNORING THEM IS THE BEST REVENGE
When you cannot have or achieve something, do not show frustration or desire. Instead, show contempt and indifference. By ignoring what you cannot have, you protect your power and avoid appearing weak or desperate.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 37: CREATE COMPELLING SPECTACLES
People are drawn to visual drama and spectacle. Create events, performances, and displays that capture the imagination. A grand spectacle distracts people, creates an aura of power, and increases your reputation.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 38: THINK AS YOU LIKE BUT BEHAVE LIKE OTHERS
Openly flaunting unconventional ideas or behavior makes you a target. Conform outwardly to the norms and customs of your environment while keeping your true thoughts and plans hidden. Share your views only with trusted friends.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 39: STIR UP WATERS TO CATCH FISH
The best way to catch fish is to stir up the water so they rise to the surface. Create confusion, chaos, or crisis, and then offer a solution. In turbulent times, people will turn to you for guidance and you can gain power.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 40: DESPISE THE FREE LUNCH
What is offered for free usually comes with a hidden cost or a hidden agenda. Never accept gifts, favors, or free lunches without considering the strings attached. What is offered freely is often a trap to create obligation.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 41: AVOID STEPPING INTO A GREAT MAN'S SHOES
What happened before you is often greater than anything you can do. When following in the footsteps of a great person, do not try to imitate or compete directly. Instead, carve your own path and make your own mark. Honor the past but build your own legacy.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 42: STRIKE THE SHEPHERD AND THE SHEEP WILL SCATTER
When you want to influence or defeat a group, find the leader, the one who holds the group together, and neutralize them. Once the shepherd is gone, the sheep will scatter and the group will fall apart.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 43: WORK ON THE HEARTS AND MINDS OF OTHERS
Coercion will only get you so far. To truly gain power over others, you must win their hearts and minds. Learn to seduce, persuade, and inspire. People who follow you willingly are more loyal and useful than those you force.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 44: DISARM AND INFURIATE WITH THE MIRROR EFFECT
Mirror your enemies -- imitate their actions and reflect their emotions back at them. This confuses and disarms them. Also use the mirror to show people their own flaws. By reflecting their own behavior back at them, you gain the upper hand.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 45: PREACH THE NEED FOR CHANGE, BUT NEVER REFORM TOO MUCH AT ONCE
People are creatures of habit and resistant to change. If you push for too much reform too quickly, you will face resistance. Advocate change but move slowly and preserve the familiar. Implement changes gradually so people can adapt.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 46: NEVER APPEAR TOO PERFECT
Appearing too perfect creates envy and fear in others. People will try to find your flaws or bring you down. Occasionally show a small weakness or flaw to appear more human and approachable. This makes people more comfortable and less threatened by you.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 47: DO NOT GO PAST THE MARK YOU AIMED FOR; IN VICTORY, LEARN WHEN TO STOP
When you have achieved your goal, stop. Success can breed overreach and arrogance. Do not push further than necessary, or you may lose what you have gained. Learn to recognize the point of victory and consolidate your gains.

author: Robert Greene
text:
LAW 48: ASSUME FORMLESSNESS
Everything in the world changes. The powerful person must be adaptable and fluid, like water. Do not rely on a fixed strategy or style. Be formless and unpredictable. Adapt to circumstances and take what you need, then move on. The ability to change is the ultimate power.
